jsonld.name: UK Stamp Duty Calculator (SDLT)
jsonld.description: Stamp Duty Land Tax for England and Northern Ireland with first-time buyer relief, additional-property, non-UK resident and corporate rates, plus non-residential property.

mainEntity.name: When did these SDLT rates start?

acceptedAnswer.text: 1 April 2025, when the nil-rate band returned to £125,000 and first-time buyer relief to £300,000 (on homes up to £500,000). The 5% additional-property surcharge has applied since 31 October 2024.

mainEntity.name: What if I replace my main home?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you are replacing your only main residence, choose Moving Home. Higher rates can apply temporarily if you still own the old home on completion day; you can then claim a refund if you sell it within three years.

mainEntity.name: Does this cover Scotland or Wales?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Scotland uses LBTT (nil rate £145,000, 8% ADS) and Wales uses LTT (nil rate £225,000, no first-time buyer relief). Use the dedicated calculators linked above.

mainEntity.name: How much stamp duty does a company pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Companies and other non-natural persons buying a dwelling for more than £500,000 usually pay a flat 17% of the whole price (19% if non-UK resident). Below that, standard rates plus the 5% surcharge apply. Qualifying businesses can claim relief from the 17% rate.

mainEntity.name: Does this cover a shop or office?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — choose Non-Residential / Mixed-Use. Slices are 0% to £150,000, 2% to £250,000 and 5% above. GOV.UK's published example is £275,000 = £3,250. Residential surcharges are not added and lease rent is not calculated.

mainEntity.name: Are these figures an HMRC assessment?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Confirm with your conveyancer. This page is a planning estimate from published bands.

mainEntity.name: When do you have to pay stamp duty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Within 14 days of the transaction's effective date, which is usually the completion date. Your solicitor or conveyancer normally files the SDLT return and pays HMRC for you.

mainEntity.name: Who pays stamp duty, the buyer or the seller?

acceptedAnswer.text: The buyer pays Stamp Duty Land Tax. The seller does not pay it.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I pay stamp duty late?

acceptedAnswer.text: Filing the return up to three months late costs £100 and filing later costs £200, with a tax-based penalty if it is still unfiled after 12 months. Interest also runs on unpaid tax from the day after it was due.

mainEntity.name: Can I get the higher rates refunded when I sell my old home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if you sell your previous main home within three years of buying the new one. For sales on or after 29 October 2018, HMRC must receive the claim within 12 months of the sale or 12 months of the new home's SDLT filing date, whichever is later.

mainEntity.name: Who counts as a first-time buyer for stamp duty?

acceptedAnswer.text: An individual who has never owned an interest in a residential property anywhere in the world, who intends to live in the home as their main residence and who pays £500,000 or less. When buying jointly, every buyer must qualify.
